column5: A gen-AI native ESG reporting platform
column6: EthicsGrade.io is a startup that offers a unique solution to Chief Sustainability Officers and other professionals who are tasked with completing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) surveys. The company operates in the ESG market, providing a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform that uses generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automate the completion of these surveys. The platform, known as EthicsAnswer, is designed to simplify and expedite the process of responding to ESG surveys. Users can ask a single question and receive an answer in seconds, or upload a full survey and receive the completed survey in less than 48 hours. The platform also provides evidence-backed responses, ensuring quick and simple verification. EthicsGrade.io's business model is based on a subscription service. Unlike free models or paid competitors, EthicsAnswer is trained solely on ESG data, ensuring that language nuances specific to ESG are recognized and responded to correctly. The platform also includes a digital ESG library where all answers are saved for easy access by the user and their organization. For those who do not have a set of published reports, EthicsGrade.io offers a "lite" version of EthicsAnswer. This allows users to save approved answers to the library and provide access to their colleagues, saving time on answering ESG questions individually. In summary, EthicsGrade.io provides a unique, AI-powered solution for automating the completion of ESG surveys, saving time and ensuring accuracy for its users. Keywords: ESG Surveys, SaaS Platform, Generative AI, Chief Sustainability Officers, Automation, Subscription Service, ESG Data, Evidence-Backed Responses, Digital ESG Library, EthicsAnswer.

column5: Sustainable solutions database for buildings
column6: Rethink Architecture operates as an educational and consulting platform in the Czech Republic, focused on promoting sustainability within architecture and construction. Founded in 2019 by Karolína Barič and Kateřina Eklová, the organization aims to bridge the knowledge gap in sustainable building practices among professionals. The founders identified a need for consolidated, accessible information, as existing know-how was fragmented and managers often did not recognize the environmental, economic, and social value of sustainable design. Both founders brought significant experience from the sustainability and real estate development sectors to their venture. Karolína Barič is an accredited specialist in LEED, BREEAM, and WELL certifications and previously worked as a sustainability coordinator and a researcher at the Czech Technical University (CTU). Kateřina Eklová has a background in residential and commercial development and is a researcher and lecturer at the Faculty of Civil Engineering at CTU. This combined expertise forms the foundation of the company's mission to educate and connect architects, investors, developers, and the public. The firm's business activities are multifaceted, primarily generating value through education and advisory services. It organizes a range of events, including lectures, workshops, seminars, and conferences targeting professionals in the construction industry as well as the general public. These events have reached over 1,000 attendees in person and garnered more than 30,000 online views. A key educational offering is the Rethink Academy, a program providing comprehensive training in sustainable development, ESG principles, and building certification standards. For a broader audience, the company publishes e-books and checklists on topics like sustainable renovation. The business model also includes consultancy services for institutions, companies, and individuals seeking guidance on sustainable architecture. Furthermore, Rethink Architecture operates the 'Database of sustainable solutions,' an online tool with free and premium tiers, offering information on sustainable technologies, suppliers, and implementation guidance. column5: At HEGG, we pride ourselves as a versatile, easy-to-use, healthy, 100% plant-based egg (a subsidiary of Hoow Foods)
column6: Hegg Foods operates as a subsidiary of the Singaporean food technology company Hoow Foods, which was established in 2018 by four graduates of the National University of Singapore. Hegg Foods itself was launched in 2021, spearheaded by CEO and co-founder Ow Yau Png, following a S$3 million pre-Series A funding round for its parent company. The creation of Hegg was a direct response to food supply chain vulnerabilities and egg shortages in Singapore that were exposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. This experience drove the founders to contribute to Singapore's "30 by 30" initiative, which aims to locally produce 30% of the nation's nutritional needs by 2030.  The company is positioned within the alternative protein market, developing and marketing plant-based egg products for consumers. Its business model revolves around the sale of these consumer-packaged goods through various channels, including e-commerce platforms like Lazada and Shopee, and physical retail. A significant milestone was achieved through a distribution agreement with Dasoon, Singapore's largest egg distributor, to place Hegg's products in the egg section of supermarket chains. The company also engages in co-development partnerships, such as the collaboration with the heritage brand Killiney Kopitiam to create an "Eggless Kaya" jam.  At the core of Hegg's product development is its parent company's proprietary AI platform, RE-GENESYS. This technology utilizes ingredient informatics to analyze and reformulate food products, enabling the rapid development of plant-based alternatives. Hegg's flagship product is a powdered, plant-based egg substitute made from ingredients like canola protein and potato fibre. This powdered format offers a shelf life of over a year without refrigeration, providing convenience and logistical advantages over liquid alternatives. Nutritionally, the product is designed to have a protein content similar to a conventional egg but with significantly less fat and no cholesterol. It is also free from common allergens like dairy, gluten, and soy. The product is versatile, intended for use in a wide range of both Western and Asian cuisines, including baking, scrambling, and steaming. column5: Developed a flexible Virtual Reality platform for therapists and healthcare professionals
column6: Amelia Virtual Care, initially established as Psious in 2014 by co-founders Xavier Palomer Ripoll and Daniel Roig Canelles, operates at the intersection of technology and mental healthcare. The company was born from Palomer's background in physics and electrical engineering, including a Master's in Bioengineering and research experience in developing devices for electrical brain stimulation. This technical expertise underpins the company's core offering. In February 2022, the company rebranded to Amelia Virtual Care, a name inspired by aviation pioneer Amelia Earhart, and appointed Afsana Akhter, a digital health veteran, as CEO to spearhead expansion.The firm provides a virtual reality (VR) platform for mental health professionals, including psychologists and therapists. This B2B SaaS model generates revenue through monthly subscription fees, granting clinicians access to its extensive library. The platform is designed to be a flexible tool, not a set program, used during patient sessions on a VR headset controlled by the therapist's computer or tablet. It supports both in-person and remote therapy, integrating with a therapist's existing workflow. The technology is grounded in established psychological paradigms like Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT), offering tools for exposure therapy, systematic desensitization, mindfulness, and relaxation techniques.The platform features over 140 virtual environments to treat a variety of conditions such as anxiety, phobias, and stress. A key feature is the ability for therapists to control and customize the virtual scenarios in real-time. For enhanced data collection, the system can incorporate biofeedback through an electrodermal response sensor that measures the patient's physiological stress levels during a session. Therapists can also track progress through session reports which may include heatmaps showing where a patient focused their attention within the virtual environment. A significant milestone occurred in April 2023, when Amelia Virtual Care announced its merger with XRHealth, a Boston-based developer of virtual treatment rooms for physical therapy. This strategic union created the largest XR therapeutics platform, combining Amelia's mental health expertise with XRHealth's capabilities in treating physical conditions like chronic pain and providing post-stroke rehabilitation. column5: Smart adaptive size-fit function that enables digital adjustment of multi-sized textile products
column6: Metamorfish is an innovative startup addressing a significant challenge in the equestrian market: the difficulty of finding riding boots that fit diverse calf sizes. Traditional riding boots come with fixed shaft sizes, leading to a mismatch between the boots and the varied calf sizes of riders. This mismatch forces manufacturers to produce numerous shaft sizes, resulting in excessive inventory and waste, which is neither cost-effective nor sustainable.Metamorfish has developed a groundbreaking solution with its three-layer craft molding textile technology. This technology allows for the creation of re-adaptable panels that can be adjusted up to 100 times in just 1.5 minutes using heat. These panels are integrated into the riding boots during the initial production phase, enabling a personalized fit for each rider. This not only enhances comfort and performance but also increases the appeal of the boots in the second-hand market due to their re-adaptability.The primary clients of Metamorfish are riding boot manufacturers looking to differentiate their products in a competitive market. By offering boots that can be easily adjusted to fit various calf sizes, these manufacturers can attract a broader customer base and reduce the need for excessive inventory. This innovation also appeals to environmentally conscious consumers who value sustainability.Metamorfish operates in the equestrian market, specifically targeting the segment of riding boot manufacturers. Its business model revolves around licensing its unique textile technology to these manufacturers. By integrating Metamorfish's panels into their products, manufacturers can offer a superior, customizable product that stands out in the market. Metamorfish generates revenue through licensing fees and possibly through a share of the sales of the enhanced riding boots.In summary, Metamorfish is revolutionizing the riding boot industry with its adaptable textile technology, providing a sustainable and customizable solution that benefits both manufacturers and riders.Keywords: re-adaptable panels, personalized fit, riding boots, equestrian market, sustainable, innovative technology, heat-activated, customizable, licensing model, enhanced resale.

column6: Molofeed, founded in 2015 by Ingmar Høgøy, is a Norwegian company addressing a critical need within the aquaculture industry for specialized larval feed. Høgøy, a chemical engineer with a background in fish farming, R&D, and process development, established the company to overcome the challenges associated with live feed for fish and shrimp larvae. The company’s core business revolves around its patented microencapsulation technology, which encloses water-soluble nutrients in a tiny, dryable shell. This process creates a powder-like feed that boasts a long shelf life and simplifies storage.The primary market for Molofeed is aquaculture hatcheries that cultivate marine finfish and shrimp. Traditionally, these hatcheries rely on live prey like Artemia and Rotifers, which are costly, pose a disease risk, and have a significant environmental footprint. Molofeed's products serve as a direct replacement, aiming to reduce or eliminate the dependency on live feeds. The company's business model is based on the development, production, and supply of these high-quality feeds directly to hatcheries. Revenue is generated through the sale of its product lines, which include specific formulations for different species and larval stages. The company received a significant investment from Aqua-Spark in 2019 to scale up production and marketing efforts.Molofeed's product portfolio includes feeds like FiskPro for marine fish and NanoPro for shrimp, designed to cover the entire hatchery and nursery process. The key feature is the microencapsulation that keeps the feed particles suspended in water until ingested, preventing nutrient leaching and water contamination. This ensures the small larvae receive adequate nutrition, leading to higher survival rates, better growth, and more uniform batches. The technology allows for the inclusion of pre-digested proteins and other water-soluble components, and can also serve as a delivery system for probiotics and immunostimulants. By repurposing seafood co-products, such as byproducts from the Norwegian cod fishing industry, Molofeed creates nutrient-dense feeds that support more sustainable aquaculture practices.Keywords: aquaculture feed, larval nutrition, microencapsulation, fish hatchery, shrimp hatchery, live feed replacement, sustainable aquaculture, marine ingredients, aquafeed technology, finfish feed, shrimp feed, larval diet, aquaculture innovation, water quality, nutrient delivery, fish farming, feed development, animal nutrition

column5: Trifilon develops, produces and sells lightweight biocomposite plastics for high performance applications
column6: Trifilon AB is a Swedish materials science company focused on producing sustainable, fiber-reinforced polymer composites to replace conventional plastics. The company's origins trace back to biocomposite research at Linköping University in 2006, which aimed to create a more recyclable alternative to carbon fiber. Seeing the commercial potential, co-founder Martin Lidstrand, who was part of the initial research, acquired the patents and established Trifilon AB in 2012 with partner Jeremiah Dutton. Lidstrand's technical background was complemented by Dutton's experience in the renewable energy sector with Siemens. The company provides biocomposite granulates that can be used in standard injection molding and extrusion machinery without requiring new equipment. Its business model revolves around selling these materials to manufacturers across diverse sectors, including automotive, consumer goods, and home furnishings. Trifilon also partners with companies globally, offering access to its proprietary production technology, including its URUK machinery, and an extensive library of over 800 material formulations to enable local production. This allows partners to manufacture Trifilon's materials using local biomass resources, tapping into the growing demand for sustainable products. Trifilon's product portfolio includes material families like BioLite®, Switch®, and Revo®, which blend natural fibers from sources like hemp and flax with polymers. These biocomposites are designed to be lighter and stronger than traditional plastics while significantly reducing the carbon footprint—in some cases by up to 90%. For instance, one of its initial commercial successes was the world's first biocomposite suitcase with EPIC Travelgear. More recently, smart home automation company Tibber used Trifilon's Revo material for its Pulse KM smart electricity reader, achieving an 80% reduction in the product's plastic-related CO2 footprint. The company's production and R&D are centralized at its facility in Nyköping, Sweden, ensuring quality control over its processes. column6: HALO offers a specialized data service focused on preventing deceased identity fraud. column5: Koatek A/S – When it’s worth doing well
column6: In 1969, in the small Danish town of Jægerspris, a craftsman named Knud Olsen started a precision mechanics workshop with just three customers. This was the beginning of Koatek A/S. Olsen built his company on a simple, yet powerful, principle: an uncompromising commitment to quality in fine-mechanical components. This foundational DNA of perfectionism proved to be a winning strategy; decades later, those same three initial clients remain customers. Koatek specializes in manufacturing highly specialized components for demanding industries like life sciences, aerospace, and the food sector, where precision is not just a goal, but a strict requirement. The company machines complex parts from a wide array of materials, including titanium and ceramics, with tolerances measured in microns. Their workshop is equipped with over 70 CNC-controlled machines, enabling everything from micro-turning to advanced laser welding and 3D measurement. A significant chapter in the company's story was written in 2019. Den Sociale Kapitalfond Invest, a private equity fund with a dual focus on financial returns and social impact, acquired a 45% stake in Koatek, becoming its largest shareholder. This move highlighted Koatek's other core value: its commitment to social responsibility, demonstrated by its focus on employing and developing skilled workers, including those with special needs. The founder's son, Bo Olsen, continued as a co-owner, ensuring the original vision remained part of the company's future.

column5: Electric truck transport-as-a-service for emerging markets
column6: OX Delivers is a technology-driven logistics company, founded in 2020 by Simon Davis and Natalie Dowsett, providing on-demand transport services in emerging markets. The company's origins trace back to a concept from philanthropist Sir Torquil Norman and Formula 1 designer Gordon Murray, who aimed to create a simple, flat-pack truck for developing countries. Recognizing that vehicle ownership was unaffordable for many, the business model evolved from selling vehicles to offering a pay-as-you-go Transport-as-a-Service (TaaS).The company launched its pilot operations in Rwanda in March 2021, initially focusing on transporting goods like coffee for smallholder farmers and traders. Clients, who previously relied on bicycles or foot travel, can book space on a truck via a mobile app or a toll-free number, paying on a kilogram-per-kilometer basis. This model significantly reduces transport time and costs, enabling entrepreneurs to access larger markets and increase their income. By late 2024, OX Delivers was serving over 5,000 customers in Rwanda, with a high rate of repeat business.At the core of the service is the purpose-built, all-terrain electric OX truck. Engineered for the rough roads of the Global South, the truck is designed to be shipped as a flat-pack (Completely Knocked Down) and assembled in-country, which lowers costs. The vehicle features a two-tonne payload and is reported to have operating costs ten times lower than diesel alternatives. A proprietary digital platform optimizes routing and truck utilization. The company has secured approximately $10 million in equity and has also received significant grant funding from entities like Innovate UK, the Advanced Propulsion Centre, and USAID. Following its success in Rwanda, OX Delivers is expanding across East Africa through franchise partnerships, with plans to enter markets in Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, and Burundi.Keywords: transport-as-a-service, electric trucks, emerging markets, logistics, last-mile delivery, pay-as-you-go transport, rural logistics, flat-pack vehicle, sustainable transport, African logistics, supply chain, e-mobility, social impact, asset financing, mobile booking, franchise model, all-terrain vehicle, economic development, agricultural logistics, Rwanda

column5: Produces sustainable footwear by combining the strongest natural fiber
column6: Earthbound, operating under the Croatian-registered company Miret d.o.o., is a footwear manufacturer focused on producing ecologically sustainable sneakers. The business was born from the founders' direct experience within the traditional footwear industry. Brothers Hrvoje and Domagoj Boljar inherited a family shoemaking business from their father, Josip Boljar, and initially produced high-end footwear for other European brands. This insider perspective revealed the industry's significant negative environmental impact, primarily from the widespread use of petroleum derivatives and chemically-treated leather, motivating them to establish a more sustainable alternative. The founders' backgrounds are complementary; Hrvoje Boljar is an industrial designer who leads product design and sustainable development, while Domagoj Boljar is an economist who manages the business operations. After a development period of approximately six years, the company launched its first products. In October 2023, the brand name transitioned from MIRET to Earthbound to better reflect its core ecological mission. The company operates on a direct-to-consumer business model, selling its products exclusively through its own webshop to maintain lower retail prices and direct communication with its customer base. Earthbound’s primary product is a line of sneakers constructed from 97% natural, bio-based materials. The company utilizes a diverse range of ten different plants and wool, including hemp, kenaf, cork, eucalyptus, and natural rubber. The wool exterior is naturally water-repellent, while the hemp lining offers breathability and odor resistance. The ergonomic footbed is crafted from cork, and the outsole from natural rubber latex. This material composition results in a CO2 footprint of 4.88 kg per pair, significantly lower than the industry average of 14 kg. The remaining 3% of the sneaker consists of synthetic glue and thread, used to ensure durability, though the company is actively researching bio-based alternatives. Earthbound's sneakers are the first in the world to receive the STANDARD 100 by OEKO-TEX label for the entire product, certifying they are free of substances harmful to human health. The company is also a certified B Corporation. The company has secured funding through various means, including grants, angel investments, and equity crowdfunding campaigns on platforms like Kickstarter and Funderbeam, raising over $1.36 million in total. Key investors include Fil Rouge Capital and the Austrian business angel association, Danube Angels. column5: AI-powered solutions optimizing electric vehicle energy efficiency
column6: VHOLA is a technology company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Kefar Sava, Israel, that specializes in improving energy efficiency for the electric vehicle (EV) industry. The company provides non-intrusive software and hardware solutions that help EV manufacturers monitor and optimize energy consumption throughout the vehicle's lifecycle, from design and development to post-production and service. The core technology integrates EMF sensors to analyze energy usage, a vehicle network listener to monitor performance, and machine learning algorithms to identify inefficiencies. This creates an "energetic fingerprint" for each vehicle component, allowing for detailed analysis and performance tracking over time. VHOLA's product suite includes e2Lab for development, e2Field for real-world testing, e2Drive for in-vehicle adaptive energy management, and e2Service for identifying efficiency losses during maintenance. The company's primary clients are electric vehicle automakers. The management team includes CEO Oren Betzaleli, COO and Founder Asaf Tsin, and several other experts in automotive technology, AI, and software development. The board of directors features notable figures such as Dr. Peter Mertens, former CTO of Audi and Volvo, and Yoni Heilbronn, a managing partner at IL Ventures. The company has received an undisclosed amount of pre-seed funding. column5: Development of biochar products for more productive and sustainable farming, animal health, and filtration
column6: Based in Porsgrunn, Norway, Standard Bio AS is a science-led company established in 2011, focused on converting bio-waste from agriculture and forestry into high-value biochar products. The company operates on a circular economy model, upcycling locally sourced, low-value biomass into environmentally friendly solutions that enhance agricultural productivity and animal health. The core of its operation is a proprietary, self-developed production method that is CO2-negative and avoids chemical treatments. This process utilizes a flameless combustion system and a rotating kiln to transform residual materials into biochar, a carbon-rich and porous material, and active-char, which has an even greater surface area. The business model is centered on a distributed and collaborative framework; Standard Bio partners with local industries to establish bio-refineries, providing the scientific knowledge, technology, and intellectual property to create profitable, sustainable value chains within local communities. Revenue is generated through these partnerships and the sale of its biocarbon-based products, which are produced by its subsidiary, Era BioCarbon AS. The company's product portfolio is tailored for various applications, including soil remediation, liquid biochar fertilizers, biochar-coated minerals, and feed supplements for animal welfare. These products are designed to improve soil fertility by increasing water and nutrient retention, enhance plant growth, and boost animal health by improving digestion and reducing methane production. Serving the agriculture, animal farming, aquaculture, and filtration markets, the company aims to provide solutions that not only improve operational efficiency for farmers but also contribute positively to the climate by sequestering carbon in the soil. The company collaborates with research institutes and universities to validate and enhance its product offerings. Standard Bio has received funding from institutional investor Sandwater to support its growth and development. column5: NanoMist techonologies utilizes nano-meter-size “mist generated by irradiation of MHz ultrasound
column6: Established in October 2002, NanoMist Technologies Co., Ltd. is a Japanese firm operating in the industrial machinery sector, specializing in ultrasonic atomization separator technology. The company's core mission originated from advancements in alcohol enrichment techniques used in traditional sake brewing. The founder, President, and CEO, Kazuo Matsuura, leveraged his background as the first son of a sake brewery, coupled with a Ph.D. in Engineering and an MBA, to establish the company. His career began at the Ozeki Research Institute before he launched NanoMist Technologies. The firm's business model centers on the research, development, design, and sale of specialized machinery. This equipment serves a diverse client base across various industries, including food and beverage processing, alcohol production, fragrance extraction, chemical purification, and environmental management. NanoMist Technologies generates revenue through the sale of its customized machines, which include ultrasonic atomizers, deodorizers, solvent and VOCs recovery machines, and water concentrators. The company's key offering is its proprietary "ultrasonic atomization technology," which provides a "steamless" method for separating chemical components. This process uses high-frequency ultrasound to generate a nano-meter-sized mist, allowing for the efficient separation, condensation, and purification of various substances from liquids without applying heat or pressure. This method presents a significant advantage over conventional techniques like distillation or evaporation by offering lower energy consumption, reduced operational costs, and a safer working environment. The technology has broad applications, from treating industrial wastewater and desalinating seawater to concentrating food products. A notable application is in Exhaust Gas Recirculation systems for the shipbuilding industry, helping vessels comply with stringent emissions regulations by reducing NOx emissions. Keywords: ultrasonic atomization, separation technology, industrial machinery, liquid compound separation, steamless purification, food processing equipment, wastewater treatment systems, chemical purification, fragrance extraction, solvent recovery, alcohol enrichment, Kazuo Matsuura, Japanese technology, marine emissions control, NOx reduction, low-energy separation

column6: Eatit is a digital healthcare provider based in Stockholm, Sweden, specializing in sustainable weight loss solutions. column5: Design, testing and manufacture of products in renewable energy and other industries
column6: Founded in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 2017 by the father-and-son team Robert and Matthew Bray, Brayfoil Technologies is a research and development firm centered on morphing wing technology. The company's inception is the culmination of 15 years of Robert Bray's research into biomimicry and composite design, inspired by a lifelong fascination with how wings produce lift. His journey led him to develop a wing capable of changing its thickness and camber simultaneously, a concept brought to fruition after years of persistent effort that began as a garage project. Robert, who serves as the Head of R&D, previously applied his design expertise as a senior managing partner at an architectural firm, while his son, Matthew Bray, holds the position of CEO and has a background in finance.Brayfoil Technologies operates by licensing its patented technology to manufacturers in the renewable energy, aerospace, sailing, and automotive industries. The core of its business is a biomimetic technology that allows structures, particularly wind turbine blades, to alter their shape in response to aerodynamic forces, much like a bird's wing. This capability addresses a significant challenge in the wind power sector: as turbine blades get longer to capture more energy, they face immense structural loads, especially during high winds and storms, which necessitates heavier and more expensive construction.The firm's primary product is a compliant, morphing aerofoil. For wind turbines, this technology enables blades to intelligently reduce these damaging loads. This load reduction is substantial, with claims of up to a 90% decrease in storm loads and a 24% reduction in operational loads. Consequently, blades can be built longer and lighter, leading to an anticipated 25% increase in annual power output and a potential 20% reduction in the levelized cost of energy without requiring additional structural reinforcement. The technology, which has undergone wind tunnel testing and CFD analysis, uses commercially viable materials and maintains a simple construction process. column6: Established in Hong Kong in 2009 by co-founders Kevin Chan and Rex Sham, Insight Robotics is a technology firm focused on proactive risk management for natural resources and infrastructure. Rex Sham, a robotics enthusiast and a 2008 computer science graduate from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, provides the technical vision, while Kevin Chan leads the business as CEO. The company offers solutions that generate and interpret data from robotic sensors to provide early-stage intelligence, enabling clients to mitigate threats before they escalate.  Insight Robotics primarily serves industries such as forestry, agriculture, and infrastructure asset management, with clients including government agencies and private plantation owners. Its business model revolves around providing end-to-end solutions, combining hardware sales with its proprietary software platform. The company has expanded its sales and marketing to key regions like China, Southeast Asia, Australia, and the Americas. To fuel its growth and research, Insight Robotics has secured significant funding, including a $2 million Series A round in 2014 and a subsequent $9 million investment in 2018 led by Beyond Ventures and Linear Capital.  The company's core offering is its Wildfire Detection System, which integrates hardware and software components. The InsightFD robot is a dual-sensor unit equipped with thermal imaging and high-definition visible-light cameras that scan 360 degrees, 24/7. It can detect fires as small as two square meters from up to 15 kilometers away, operating effectively in various weather conditions. This hardware is powered by an AI-Engine for on-site edge computing, which uses machine learning to reduce false alarms. All data is transmitted to Insight Globe, a geospatial intelligence system (GIS) platform. This software provides real-time 2D and 3D maps, pinpoints fire coordinates, sends alerts to personnel, and warehouses historical data for risk analysis and mitigation planning. Beyond wildfire detection, the company also provides aerial survey services using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for applications like monitoring crop health and has adapted its thermal detection technology for public health screenings. column6: PropEco Ltd, established in 2020 by founder Christopher Browne, operates as a specialized data and analytics provider for the UK property market, with a distinct focus on climate and environmental risks. This platform delivers property-level risk analysis, covering hazards such as flooding, subsidence, and coastal erosion, while also providing insights into energy performance certificate (EPC) ratings and local amenities. The business model is structured around a B2B subscription service, offering access to its data via an API. This allows clients to integrate PropEco's insights directly into their existing workflows and decision-making processes, thereby enhancing risk management and identifying opportunities for sustainable property investment.Significant milestones for the company include securing a pre-seed funding round in 2021, which enabled the initial development and launch of its platform. column5: Autonomous façade technology that transforms conventional building envelopes into climate-adaptive, energy-saving skins for sustainable urban construction
column6: Sky-Walls Ltd. is a cutting-edge startup revolutionizing energy efficiency in high-rise and commercial buildings through its innovative Autonomous Facade Module (AFM). This patented technology transforms traditional double or triple-glazed curtain walls into intelligent, self-sustaining façades that dynamically adapt to changing climate conditions without relying on external energy sources. Powered by integrated solar panels, the AFM continuously monitors indoor and outdoor environments to adjust its thermal insulation and solar heat gain properties in real time. This adaptive capability maximizes solar heat gain during winter months to reduce heating demands and minimizes heat penetration in summer to lower cooling costs, resulting in up to a 30% reduction in HVAC energy consumption. By seamlessly integrating AI-driven adaptability with energy self-sufficiency, Sky-Walls offers a scalable, cost-effective solution that addresses the significant energy inefficiencies of modern glass towers and urban buildings. The technology not only contributes to substantial energy savings and carbon footprint reduction but also enhances occupant comfort and building performance. Supported by the Israeli Innovation Authority and backed by recent investment rounds, Sky-Walls is positioned as a key player in the climate tech and green building sectors, aiming to reshape urban landscapes with smarter, sustainable façades that respond autonomously to environmental changes. Their work exemplifies the intersection of deep tech and renewable energy equipment manufacturing, leveraging advanced optics, AI, and solar technologies to drive the future of sustainable architecture and smart cities.

column5: A large-scale biorefinery launched by SCA and St1, promising new ways to explore sustainable energy innovation
column6: Biorefinery Östrand AB operates as a joint venture, equally owned by the Swedish forest industry company SCA and the Finnish energy company St1. This partnership leverages the strengths of both parent companies: SCA, as Europe's largest private forest owner, provides a steady supply of feedstock, while St1 contributes its expertise in the fuel sector and energy transition. The collaboration between SCA and St1 is not new; they previously partnered on the Gothenburg Biorefinery, which began operations in early 2024.The core business of Biorefinery Östrand is the large-scale production of advanced biofuels, specifically Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and renewable naphtha. The project is positioned to address the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, particularly the aviation industry, which faces ambitious mandates to increase the use of SAF. The planned facility, to be located adjacent to SCA's Östrand pulp mill in Timrå, Sweden, will have a production capacity of 300,000 tons of biofuels, including 185,000 tons of SAF and 50,000 tons of naphtha. Beyond its climate benefits, the project aims to enhance Sweden's self-sufficiency in sustainable fuel production.The production process is what sets the facility apart. It will be the first commercial-scale deployment of a solid biomass-to-liquid (BTL) pathway, combining established technologies like gasification and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis in a novel configuration. The process uses by-products from the forest industry, such as sawdust and bark, which are considered sustainable feedstocks under the EU's RED III directive. These solid biomass materials are converted into syngas, which is then transformed into liquid hydrocarbons. To maximize the yield and efficiency, the process incorporates green hydrogen produced on-site via an electrolyzer powered by renewable electricity. This integration of different technologies is a key aspect of the project. The strategic location next to SCA's pulp mill allows for significant operational synergies, including the direct transfer of bark feedstock via conveyor belt and shared infrastructure for energy and water management.The project has achieved significant milestones, including securing environmental permits and a grant agreement of approximately €167 million from the EU Innovation Fund, contingent on a final investment decision. The project officially started on January 1, 2024, with a target entry into operation by June 30, 2029. The development is proceeding in stages, with site preparation currently underway while dialogues with suppliers continue. Once operational, it is expected to create 60 direct and 660 indirect jobs, contributing to the local economy.Keywords: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), biorefinery, renewable energy, biomass-to-liquid (BTL), Fischer-Tropsch, St1, SCA, green hydrogen, renewable naphtha, biofuels, decarbonization, aviation industry, circular economy, forest residues, wood pellets, syngas, energy transition, EU Innovation Fund, electrofuels, clean technology, sustainable fuels, biomass gasification, renewable diesel, Swedish industry

column6: Thalia Psychotherapy is a for-profit social enterprise, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, with the mission to integrate mental health services into everyday life across Africa. Mercy Mwende's experience in the healthcare sector, where she identified the unmet need for mental health support among patients seeking physical care, was a key inspiration for the company's creation.The organization operates in Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, and Malawi, with a focus on making mental health care accessible and affordable, particularly for marginalized groups. Thalia addresses the significant gap in mental healthcare in Africa, a continent with fewer than two mental health workers per 100,000 people. Its business model involves embedding mental health services within existing healthcare systems, collaborating with governments, hospitals, schools, and workplaces. A key strategy is integrating standardized mental health screenings into primary healthcare facilities, having already implemented this in over 6,500 health centers and conducted more than 7 million screenings. This allows for early detection and intervention, viewing individuals holistically.Thalia leverages a blend of technology and traditional therapies, utilizing AI-powered screening tools, mobile assessments, and digital platforms to offer cost-effective and scalable solutions. One of their key offerings is an AI-powered chatbot for initial assessments and therapy sessions. The company has established Africa's largest network of over 6,000 therapists and offers specialized services like 'Ajala,' an anonymous support hotline for men. Revenue is generated through these services and by pioneering results-based financing structures. This innovative model aims to attract investment from African pension funds, positioning mental health as a commercially viable and sustainable market. column5: Tezted Oy is innovating the way tick-borne diseases are diagnosed at a 90% cost reduction for the patient with their Tickplex products
column6: Tezted Oy is a Finnish biotechnology firm established in 2016, operating from Jyväskylä. The company is focused on the development and commercialization of in-vitro diagnostic tests for infectious diseases, with a particular emphasis on tick-borne illnesses. The company was co-founded by Kunal Garg and Leona Gilbert. Their journey began at the University of Jyväskylä in 2014 within Leona Gilbert's research team, which has a two-decade history of studying autoimmune diseases. Observing the significant negative impact of tick-borne diseases on patients' quality of life and the limitations of existing diagnostic tools that primarily focused on Lyme disease, they initiated a study. Their research, which profiled thousands of patient samples against various pathogens, revealed that a high percentage of individuals with tick-borne illnesses suffer from multiple infections simultaneously. This finding highlighted the market need for a more comprehensive diagnostic solution, leading to the creation of Tezted. Tezted's business model centers on providing diagnostic solutions to clinical laboratories. The company develops, manufactures, and sells CE-IVD-marked, ELISA-based diagnostic kits. These kits are produced under ISO 13485:2016 certified manufacturing processes. The firm generates revenue through the sale of these kits, having received initial funding for research and commercial viability analysis from the Schwartz Foundation and TEKES, the Finnish Funding Agency for Technology and Innovation. The company's core product is TICKPLEX®, a diagnostic test designed to simultaneously detect multiple tick-borne pathogens from a single patient sample. This addresses a major shortcoming of conventional testing, which often screens only for Lyme disease, potentially missing co-infections. TICKPLEX® can identify approximately 15 different pathogens, which can significantly reduce testing costs compared to running multiple individual tests. A key feature of the test is its ability to detect both the common spirochete and the less-detected persistent circular forms of Borrelia, the bacteria responsible for Lyme disease. The product line includes TICKPLEX® BASIC, which focuses on various species and forms of Borrelia, and TICKPLEX® PLUS, which expands to cover co-infections like Babesiosis and Bartonellosis. column5: Beskow von Post are experts in the upcycling of discarded company textiles
column6: Beskow von Post, established in Stockholm in 2021, operates within the circular economy, specifically targeting the textile waste sector. The company was founded by Susanne Beskow and Caroline von Post, who bring a complementary blend of expertise to the venture. Beskow is a graduate of Beckmans College of Design and has an extensive background as a textile designer, creating collections for various brands and workwear for prominent companies like Finnair and Securitas. Von Post holds a master's degree in systems ecology from Stockholm University and has a history as an environmental consultant and with environmental organizations, including founding the upcycling company Stormie Poodle in 2008. Their combined experience in design, sustainability, and upcycling forms the foundation of the company. The core business of Beskow von Post is transforming discarded workwear and industrial textiles into a new, climate-smart raw material through a patent-pending upcycling process. This material is standardized and digitally traceable, addressing a key challenge in textile recycling. The company collaborates with corporate clients, such as the textile service company Elis, to manage their textile waste. In one notable project, approximately five pairs of discarded work trousers were repurposed to create one new unisex overshirt. This B2B model not only provides a solution for textile waste but also helps client companies reduce their climate footprint and strengthen their brand image around sustainability. The firm's products are tangible outcomes of its service, demonstrating the potential of upcycled materials. For instance, Beskow von Post was commissioned to design and produce new staff uniforms for Sweden's Nationalmuseum using discarded garments and leftover fabrics. This business model involves designing and manufacturing new, high-value products from what was once considered waste. All production emphasizes social responsibility, with manufacturing done in collaboration with social enterprises. The company has received recognition for its approach, including the Design S award, which celebrates innovative and sustainable solutions. column5: Chilean solar energy distribution platform
column6: Ciudad Luz is a Chilean company specializing in distributed solar energy generation, positioning itself as an Energy Service Company (ESCO). Founded in 2013 by brothers Tomás, Matías, and Andrés Steinacker, along with José Luis Opazo, the company emerged from the founders' vision to democratize solar energy in Chile. While studying abroad, the Steinacker brothers observed the widespread adoption of solar panels and recognized the immense untapped potential in sunny Chile. Initially exploring large-scale solar plants, they pivoted to a distributed generation model to overcome the significant capital barriers for end-users. The company's core business revolves around a "Solar as a Service" (SaaS) model, where it finances, designs, installs, operates, and maintains photovoltaic (PV) systems for residential, commercial, and industrial clients. Revenue is primarily generated through long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), typically 15 to 20 years, where clients buy the generated energy from Ciudad Luz at a rate lower than the grid price, ensuring immediate savings without any upfront investment. At the end of the contract term, ownership of the solar installation is transferred to the client. The company serves a diverse client base, including the agro-industrial, retail, real estate, and educational sectors. A key strategic milestone was the 2018 joint venture with Empresas Gasco, creating Gasco Luz, a vehicle to scale the ESCO model for commercial and industrial projects in Chile. This was followed by an expansion into Colombia. For residential projects, Ciudad Luz has established alliances with financial institutions like Banco Santander to offer "green credit" options and participates in private investment funds to facilitate installations with no initial cost. A critical component of its service is the proprietary "Cloud Solar" technology platform, developed with the help of a Newton-Picarte Chile UK grant, which manages the distributed energy assets. This end-to-end service, which removes the financial and operational burden from the customer, constitutes its main value proposition. By 2022, the B-Corp certified company had an operational portfolio of 25MW and a development pipeline exceeding 50MW, backed by over 60 shareholders. column6: Navetas Energy Management, founded in 2008 by former Actaris Metering Systems executives Chris Saunders and Chris Shelley, operated in the energy management sector, focusing on providing solutions for both businesses and consumers to monitor and reduce energy consumption. The company's chairman, Mike Mannering, brought extensive experience from the international energy markets. Navetas originated as a spin-out from the University of Oxford, transforming a university concept into its core technology. The firm's core offering was an energy disaggregation technology. This system utilized advanced software algorithms and artificial intelligence on a low-cost hardware platform, which could be integrated into products like smart meters. From a single point on the electricity supply, the technology could identify and calculate the energy consumption of individual appliances within a home. This provided consumers with detailed, itemized information about their energy usage, aiming to empower them to make informed decisions and reduce waste. The associated consumer-facing product, known as Loop, featured an engaging user interface and a robust back-end to handle large volumes of data, presenting energy consumption in an accessible format. The Loop app, available for free to households with smart meters, analyzes usage data to help users track consumption, identify waste, and understand appliance running costs. Navetas's business model involved both direct-to-consumer offerings and strategic partnerships within the energy industry. The company secured significant venture capital from Swarraton Partners and Naxos Private Equity upon its launch. A pivotal moment came in 2012 when it secured a £5 million investment from Sensus, a smart grid technology firm, for a 15% stake. This deal included an exclusive license agreement to integrate Navetas's disaggregation technology into Sensus's next-generation smart meters for the U.S. market. The company also had a technology partnership with Texas Instruments to embed its monitoring technology on their processor platforms. UK Government records indicate that Navetas Energy Management Ltd. is now dissolved. However, the Loop brand and its energy-saving app continue to operate, developed by Trust Power Ltd. column5: An application designed to allow ethnic grocery shopping from the comfort of home
column6: Bakkal Corporation operates as a business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) marketplace specifically focused on the ethnic grocery sector. The company's platform is designed to connect consumers with local, small grocery stores that offer international and ethnic food products which are often difficult to find in mainstream chain supermarkets. The company was founded in 2021 by Murat Karslioglu, Ahmet Altug, and Robert Calgav. CEO Murat Karslioglu, a serial entrepreneur with over two decades of experience in the IT industry, including storage, distributed systems, and enterprise hardware, was inspired to create Bakkal after his own experiences struggling to find familiar Turkish food products after moving to the U.S. Recognizing that this was a common problem for many immigrant communities and seeing a gap in the market during the pandemic, he launched the venture to digitize the ethnic grocery supply chain. Bakkal's business model resembles that of larger platforms like Instacart but is tailored for the niche market of ethnic foods. column5: Resiclo is developing plastics recycling to increase the recycling rate through advanced chemical recycling of difficult to recycle plastics
column6: Resiclo Oy, established in 2020, is a Finnish circular economy firm focused on advanced chemical recycling of plastics that are otherwise difficult to process. The company was founded by Tomi Nyman, Kimmo Kontuniemi, Paul Shine, and Yrjo Laakso. The founders' backgrounds are complementary, with Nyman's experience in bioplastics and chemical recycling programs, Kontuniemi's entrepreneurial focus on sales and networking, Shine's extensive research in chemical recycling, and Laakso's expertise in petrochemical processes.The company's primary business involves developing chemical recycling sites to convert hard-to-recycle plastic waste into a chemically recycled raw material, known as pyrolysis oil. This oil serves as a substitute for fossil crude oil and can be utilized by the petrochemical industry to produce new, high-quality plastics suitable for demanding applications, including food packaging. The process addresses a significant market need, as only a small fraction of global plastic waste is currently recycled. By providing a solution for mixed and certain thermoplastics incompatible with mechanical recycling, Resiclo aims to increase the overall plastic recycling rate and reduce reliance on virgin fossil fuels.A significant milestone for Resiclo was the partnership formed in 2022 with Lamor Corporation, a global environmental solutions provider. This collaboration led to the creation of a joint venture, Lamor Resiclo Oy, to construct Finland's first industrial-scale chemical recycling plant in Kilpilahti, Porvoo. The initial phase targeted an annual capacity of 10,000 tons. In March 2025, Lamor Corporation acquired the remaining 30% stake in the joint venture from Resiclo, taking full ownership of the chemical recycling business. column5: Develops distributed mini-refineries that extract precious minerals and rare earth elements from e-waste
column6: BlueOak Resources, established in 2010 by co-founders Priv Bradoo and Bryce Goodman, was a venture-backed company focused on urban mining to recover high-value metals from electronic waste. The company's business model was inspired by the steel industry's mini-mill disruption, aiming to create a distributed network of refineries to process e-waste domestically. This strategy intended to provide a U.S.-based solution for the growing e-waste problem, which was often exported, leading to environmental issues and the loss of valuable resources. Co-founder and CEO Privahini Bradoo brought a unique blend of scientific and business acumen to the company. She earned a PhD in Neurogenetics from the University of Auckland before attending Harvard Business School as a Fulbright Scholar. Her background in science fueled her passion for developing clean technologies. Co-founder Bryce Goodman, a former precious metals commodity trader and graduate of Singularity University, complemented this with his expertise in technology, philosophy, and economics. His work often focuses on the intersection of emerging technologies and global challenges. The company's core service involved deploying mini-refineries that used capital-efficient processes to extract precious metals like gold, silver, copper, and palladium from discarded electronics such as circuit boards and cell phones. BlueOak planned to work with electronics recycling organizations, processing their collected scrap for a fee and returning the recovered value. In a major milestone, BlueOak secured $35 million in project financing in June 2014 to construct its first commercial-scale refinery in Osceola, Arkansas. This facility was designed to process approximately 15 million pounds of e-waste annually using a plasma arc furnace supplied by Tetronics. However, the facility encountered significant operational challenges, including a furnace failure in November 2015 that resulted in a fire and a subsequent $10.5 million insurance lawsuit. Following these setbacks and a lengthy contract dispute, the Osceola plant was closed, its assets were auctioned off, and the site was later acquired by smelting giant Glencore in 2019. column5: Indoor vertical farmers delivering fresh greens
column6: Plenty.ag is a pioneering company in the indoor vertical farming industry. This innovative business focuses on growing fresh, healthy, and flavorful produce using significantly less space and fewer resources compared to traditional farming methods. By stacking plants vertically in controlled indoor environments, Plenty can produce crops year-round, regardless of external weather conditions. This method not only maximizes space but also reduces water usage and eliminates the need for harmful pesticides and GMOs (genetically modified organisms).Plenty's primary clients include grocery stores, restaurants, and direct consumers who prioritize sustainability and high-quality produce. The company operates in the agricultural technology market, which is rapidly growing as consumers and businesses alike seek more sustainable and efficient ways to produce food.The business model of Plenty revolves around the sale of its fresh produce. By leveraging advanced farming techniques, Plenty can offer a consistent supply of high-quality fruits and vegetables. This reliability and quality allow the company to command premium prices for its products. Additionally, Plenty's efficient use of resources and space translates into lower operational costs, further enhancing its profitability.Plenty makes money by selling its produce directly to consumers through online platforms and partnerships with grocery stores and restaurants. The company also benefits from its strong brand reputation for sustainability and quality, which helps attract a loyal customer base willing to pay a premium for its products.In summary, Plenty.ag is revolutionizing the way we grow and consume produce by offering a sustainable, efficient, and high-quality alternative to traditional farming. column5: Helps employers, health plans, at-risk providers and government programs lower costs, increase engagement and produce better health outcomes
column6: ConsejoSano, founded in 2014 by Abner Mason, Alex Denny, and Jamie Morganstern, operated as a patient engagement platform targeting multicultural and underserved populations within the U.S. healthcare system. The company was later rebranded as SameSky Health. Founder and CEO Abner Mason's background is deeply rooted in health policy and advocacy; he served as a Chief Policy Advisor to Massachusetts governors, was appointed to the Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS by President George W. Bush, and founded the Workplace Wellness Council of Mexico. This experience informed the company's mission to address health disparities by building trust with patients. The firm's business model focused on providing culturally and linguistically tailored communication and care navigation services to health plans, providers, and health systems. Its clients were primarily entities serving Medicaid and Medicare populations, aiming to increase engagement and improve health outcomes for their members. ConsejoSano generated revenue by offering its platform and services to these large healthcare organizations, helping them connect with diverse patient groups. By 2020, the company's platform was utilized by four of the top five managed care plans in the country. The core service was a technology platform that combined multi-channel communication tools—like text messaging, phone calls, and email—with data analytics and a multilingual care team. This platform used millions of cultural data points to create personalized patient outreach in over 25 languages. This approach moved beyond simple translation to ensure messaging was culturally relevant, thereby building trust and improving patient navigation of a complex healthcare system. The service assisted with scheduling appointments, understanding benefits, and connecting patients to community services, effectively addressing social determinants of health. The company raised a total of $24 million over several funding rounds, including a $17.1 million Series B in September 2020, before being acquired by Included Health. column5: Multi-vehicle battery swapping infrastructure for electric fleets
column6: Founded in 2021 and based in Ourense, Spain, VI&GO provides battery swapping infrastructure for electric vehicles with removable batteries. The company, whose legal name is AUVI SMART ELECTRIC, S.L., was started by Ignacio Iglesias and aims to address the challenge of limited access to electric mobility for companies with light vehicle fleets, such as motorcycles and bicycles.  VI&GO's core product is a network of modular battery exchange stations, or hubs, combined with a proprietary management software. This system is designed to be versatile, supporting various electric vehicle makes and models, which allows for a flexible solution for diverse fleets. The software enables fleet operators to monitor battery status in real-time, optimize usage, ensure continuous availability, and manage performance. The platform also provides key performance indicators for the business through its interface or an API integration. Key features include Ai Charge, which adapts charging to energy demand, robust and modular station design, and the ability to use renewable energy sources for recharging.  The company's business model targets fleet operators, offering them a way to reduce vehicle downtime and operational costs associated with conventional charging. By providing a quick and accessible battery swapping service, VI&GO enhances the operational efficiency of electric fleets. The company has participated in incubation programs such as IX INCUVI Emprende and the High Tech Auto incubator, and has received support from entities like EIT KIC Urban Mobility.
